issues.legal_issue: A temporary injunction issued in a suit does not automatically revive when the suit is restored after dismissal for default.
material_facts: A temporary injunction had been granted in a suit.
The suit was dismissed for default and later restored.
The lower court treated the injunction as having revived on restoration without a fresh express order.
issues.conclusion: The injunction did not automatically revive on restoration of the suit; an express order is required to revive it.
issues.legal_principle: The Code of Civil Procedure distinguishes incidental proceedings, which aid the final adjudication and whose ancillary orders may revive with the suit, from supplemental proceedings, which provide separate protective relief in the interest of justice. An injunction is supplemental in nature, so it requires a fresh order after restoration unless the court expressly directs its revival. The judgment refers to Sections 94 and 148 and Orders 38, 39 and 40 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and relies on Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das concerning the need for statutory authority to grant injunctions. It discusses and distinguishes decisions including Chunni Kuar v. Dwarka Prasad and Gangappa v. Boregowda, while rejecting the view that an injunction automatically revives as an ancillary order.

rule.if: civil_suit_dismissed_then_restored and temporary_injunction_granted_in_suit and injunction_is_supplemental_order and no_express_revival_order

predicates.civil_suit_dismissed_then_restored: A civil suit was dismissed and later restored.
predicates.temporary_injunction_granted_in_suit: A court granted a temporary injunction in the suit.
predicates.injunction_is_supplemental_order: The injunction operates as a separate protective order rather than as an order aiding the final adjudication of the suit.
predicates.no_express_revival_order: The court did not expressly direct that the injunction revive when the suit was restored.
predicates.injunction_does_not_automatically_revive: The injunction does not regain effect solely because the suit is restored.

issues.definition: When a suit dismissed and later restored had a temporary injunction treated as a supplemental order, that injunction does not regain effect solely on restoration if the court did not expressly direct its revival.
